title: Filling the Gap: The Consequences of Collaborator Loss in Corporate R&D
eligible_reason: Matched event-study DiD, not a TWFE staggered design. Treated inventors (co-inventor died unexpectedly, 845 deaths spread over 1980-2013) are compared with inventors linked to a matched 'pseudo-deceased' co-inventor. Equation (1) includes inventor FE, inventor-age FE and deceased-co-inventor (match group) x relative-year FE; calendar-year FE are omitted as collinear. This is a matching-based, stacked-by-event design with match-group-by-relative-time FE (adopted explicitly, following Bernstein et al. 2022, to address the Roth et al. 2023 TWFE critique), and it adds age FE as a further nonredundant set. PROTOCOL excludes matching-based DiD, stacked designs and additional nonredundant FE; no unstacked TWFE with calendar-time FE appears in the main text (Table A5.7 cols 1-2 in the Online Appendix drop the match-group x relative-year FE but remain matched with age FE).
design_notes: Data: INV-BIO ADIAB 1980-2014 (IAB social-security records linked to DPMA patents), ~150,000 inventors; sample 3,471 treated and 3,215 control remaining inventors, 124,168 inventor-year observations, 856 clusters (employer of the (pseudo-)deceased co-inventor). Window t = -11..8 around the (pseudo-)death year. Outcomes: patent counts and citation-weighted patent counts, winsorized at 95th percentile. Table 3 static DiD: col 1 collaborator loss -0.027 (0.022); col 2 internal 0.024 (0.029) vs external -0.081 (0.034); cols 3-4 citation-weighted -0.054 (0.030), 0.028 (0.038), -0.141 (0.044). Figure 3 event study: relative-year bins grouped two years, baseline t = -1, coefficients in Online Appendix Table A4.1.

screener_notes: INV-BIO ADIAB are confidential German social-security microdata accessible only through the IAB Research Data Centre (FDZ) on-site / remote execution; the MS supplemental 'data files' are unlikely to contain the microdata. Even if the design were admitted, the control group is a matched pseudo-event sample rather than not-yet-treated units, so the CSA/BJS mapping would be non-standard.
